Because the birds remain free to ignore us, every visit feels less like success than permission, granted briefly by a chickadee with one seed in its beak.
The garden teaches scale gently: a fallen sunflower shell can matter to an ant, a sparrow, a mouse, and the person sweeping the step after lunch.
No sermon could improve the sight of a robin listening in wet soil while, three feet away, goldfinches quarrel softly over a feeder we cleaned before dawn.
